title: Atomized OpenAI ChatCompletions request normalizer for mixed-client workloads
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a request normalization layer that converts diverse OpenAI Chat Completions request shapes into a single atomized Redwood internal request schema while preserving semantic fidelity for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. The normalizer must: canonicalize message roles and metadata, split compound messages into token-prefix friendly chunks to expose KV/prefix caching opportunities, extract and materialize function_call intents into explicit tool invocation descriptors, map OpenAI streaming delta fragments into Redwood incremental delta events, preserve stop/max_tokens/temperature/penalty semantics and translate them to runtime execution knobs, generate deterministic idempotency/reconciliation keys, and validate or reject unsupported legacy fields with clear error codes. It should be tolerant of partial function schemas (graceful fallback to best-effort), and emit structured telemetry for routing/quality debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover canonicalization of message roles, name/metadata propagation, and edge cases (empty content, long system prompts).

Streaming integration test that starts with OpenAI-style SSE fragments (delta messages + function_call partials) and verifies Redwood streaming output preserves event order, token boundaries, and final assembled function arguments.

Function calling path: requests with function_call: 'auto'|'none'|{name} are normalized to explicit tool invocation descriptors; tool schema matching succeeds or a documented fallback is applied and logged.
Idempotency: repeated identical client requests produce identical normalization fingerprints and safe retry behavior with deduplication in the runtime harness.
Performance: end-to-end normalization adds <2ms p95 overhead for typical small requests and <8ms p95 for payloads with large function schemas (measured in CI).
Backward compatibility: legacy clients missing 'name' on messages or using deprecated fields are accepted and translated, with a deprecation warning emitted in response headers and telemetry.
Docs: compatibility guide and SDK adapter examples updated and a migration snippet added to the OpenAI-compat README.
implementation_notes: Parser: tokenizes messages into (role, name?, content) atoms. Retain original ordering and source metadata to attach to telemetry traces.

Function_call handling: three-mode support (auto, none, explicit). When explicit, verify name exists in provided function list; if args stream in partial tokens, buffer until balanced JSON detected or flush heuristics after timeout.
Streaming: map OpenAI 'delta' SSE frames to Redwood incremental frames. Maintain event IDs for reordering detection and include 'final' marker when 'finish_reason' present.
Prefix/KV cache hints: annotate normalized request with prefix boundaries and probable rolling key signatures derived from leading messages (system + first user chunk).
Error mapping: return structured error codes (COMPAT_INVALID_SCHEMA, COMPAT_PARTIAL_FUNCTION, COMPAT_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD) and include reconciler-friendly metadata to assist client SDKs.

Telemetry: add tags for client_type (openai-sdk, redwood-sdk, legacy-proxy), function_call_mode, normalized_token_count, and fingerprint. Emit span for normalization step with sampling for large payloads.
Security: validate function schemas to avoid unsafe patterns (e.g., uninterpreted shell commands in descriptions). Flag for security review if function definitions include exec-like fields.
Testing: include fuzzing harness for malformed function schemas and streaming fragmentation patterns, and an e2e scenario that exercises Dedicated + fallback routing to hosted model variants.
steps: Design spec: finalize canonical request schema and normalization rules
Prototype parser and streaming adapter in go/redwood-compat repo
Cross-team review: API/SDK/Console/Runtime review for edge cases
Integrate into request ingress code path behind feature flag
Unit & integration tests + CI performance benchmarks
Canary rollout in staging then limited production (10% traffic) with detailed telemetry
Post-rollout bake, iterate on fallback heuristics
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose atomized request model (role+name+content atoms) over monolithic JSON transform to preserve prefix caching signals. - Decision by: Liam Chen, Priya Nair
2026-03-04: Buffering heuristic for streamed function_call args: accept bracket-balance + 200ms idle flush as default; allow per-customer override. - Decision by: Runtime team

2026-03-08: Error codes standardized with SDK leads to enable clear retry semantics; COMPAT_PARTIAL_FUNCTION treated as warning if runtime can synthesize a safe fallback. - Decision by: API and SDK PMs
